evals.name: bare-invocation-runs-read-only-check
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only check action (the default) and reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table with one remediation line per FAIL, writing nothing.
expectations: Defaults to check when no argument is given
Reads the clean skill and its bundled scripts as the source of truth for prerequisites rather than reciting SKILL.md
Makes no configuration change and never prompts when the action is given

evals.name: apply-is-guidance-only
evals.expected_output: Runs the check first, then points at each remediation without writing any consumer-project configuration.
expectations: Writes nothing — the plugin owns no consumer-project configuration
Names the native userConfig toggle as the only tunable

evals.name: exec-form-wired-hook-registration-fails-step-one
evals.prompt: /disk-hygiene:setup check on a machine whose hooks/hooks.json registers the wired hooks as "command": "bash" with an args array.
evals.expected_output: Step 1 FAILs on the registration shape itself: exec form resolves `bash` on PATH, which on Windows finds the WSL relay System32\bash.exe, the launch fails, and a failed hook launch is non-blocking so the guard silently enforces nothing.
expectations: Fails on the bare interpreter name in command, not on the machine's environment
Does NOT report the problem as a PATH-ordering issue and does NOT recommend reordering PATH or setting CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH
Names the fix as command node with hooks/exec-bash.mjs first in args, then hooks/run-python-hook.sh

evals.name: missing-bash-fails-the-launcher-probe
evals.prompt: /disk-hygiene:setup check on a Windows machine with no Git Bash installed and no bash.exe on PATH outside System32.
evals.expected_output: FAILs the bash probe: no bash resolves in the order the exec-bash.mjs header lists, so every hook fails to launch, the user sees a hook error notice, the guard is not enforced, and the model is not told.
expectations: Reads the resolution order from hooks/exec-bash.mjs rather than reciting it
Names CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH, a Git for Windows install, or a bash.exe on PATH outside System32, Sysnative and WindowsApps as the remediation
Still reports the wired-hook registration shape as correct when it is

evals.name: disabled-toggle-keeps-guard-launch-failures-at-fail
evals.prompt: /disk-hygiene:setup check with disk_hygiene_enabled set to false and python3 resolving to the zero-length WindowsApps alias stub.
evals.expected_output: Most prerequisite absences downgrade to INFO under a disabled toggle, but every step-1 and step-2 failure stays FAIL — a guard that never launches cannot read or enforce the configured false, so the fail-open is most dangerous in exactly this configuration.
expectations: Does not downgrade a step-1 or step-2 failure to INFO because the plugin is disabled
Treats the store-alias-stub alias-probe verdict as a guard-launch failure
Notes that re-enabling restores FAIL semantics for the downgraded probes

evals.name: python-below-floor-fails-closed
evals.prompt: /disk-hygiene:setup check where python3 launches successfully but reports version 3.6.
evals.expected_output: FAILs on the parsed MIN_PYTHON floor from skills/clean/scripts/hygiene.py rather than accepting a successful launch as proof the guard can run.
expectations: Derives the required version from the MIN_PYTHON constant, not a copy in the README
Treats a launching-but-too-old interpreter as unproven guard execution and fails closed
Explains that a version probe proves only that something executes
